Consider the following hard K-means clustering problem with five points: A (1, 2), B (2, 3), C (6, 7), D (8, 8), and E (7, 6). Consider the number of clusters to be K = 2 and the initial centroids to be C 1 = (0, 0) and C 2 = (7, 7). After how many iterations will the algorithm terminate and what will be the final centroids?
Which of the following is/are True?
options: K-means algorithm requires the initial centroids to be chosen randomly.
K-means algorithm may not find the globally optimal solution.
The complexity of the K-means algorithm is polynomial with respect to the number of data points and clusters.
K-means algorithm can be used for clustering data points in higher- dimensional spaces.
correct_answer: K-means algorithm requires the initial centroids to be chosen randomly.
The complexity of the K-means algorithm is polynomial with respect to the number of data points and clusters.
K-means algorithm can be used for clustering data points in higher- dimensional spaces.
